note: Every compound and blend in the Library, with the status, evidence grade, goals and lab list of the ones that have a fact sheet. Written by scripts/build_library.mjs for Sig (miraclehealth.us/ai) and its screen.

items.name: AOD-9604
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A lab-made piece of human growth hormone, taken for fat loss. It was developed as an obesity drug, but its main weight-loss trial failed. Not approved.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: Anastrozole
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription pill that stops the body making estrogen. Approved for hormone-sensitive breast cancer after menopause. Also studied in men with low testosterone, which it isn't approved for.

before: Pregnancy test if pregnancy is possible
during: Bone density at intervals
Cholesterol periodically
Men (off-label): testosterone and estradiol

items.name: Armodafinil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for sleep disorders; Schedule IV
items.summary: One of the two mirror-image forms of modafinil, a prescription drug that keeps people with sleep disorders awake. Also taken for focus, an unapproved use with little direct evidence in healthy people.

items.name: Ashwagandha
items.status_label: Dietary supplement (banned in Denmark)
items.summary: An herb from Ayurvedic medicine (Withania somnifera). Extracts of its root are taken mainly to ease stress and anxiety and to sleep better.

items.name: BPC-157
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding not yet allowed
items.summary: A small piece of a protein first found in human stomach juice. People take it to heal tendons, muscles and the gut. Most of the evidence comes from rodents.

before: Complete blood count and comprehensive metabolic panel (includes liver enzymes and glucose) as a general health check

items.name: Berberine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A plant compound from goldenseal, barberry and Oregon grape. Taken mainly to lower blood sugar and for weight loss.

before: Fasting glucose and HbA1c if you are using it for blood sugar
during: HbA1c or glucose checks to judge the effect, especially alongside diabetes medicines

items.name: Bronchogen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A tiny peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for the lungs and airways. So far the evidence is limited to studies in cells and rats.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: CJC-1295 no DAC (Mod GRF 1-29)
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A modified copy of the hormone that triggers the release of growth hormone. Sold as a 'research chemical' to raise growth hormone. The only evidence comes from related peptides.

before: General health check with a doctor
during: IGF-1
Fasting glucose or HbA1c

items.name: CJC-1295 with DAC
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A long-acting, lab-made version of the hormone that triggers the release of growth hormone. Taken to raise growth hormone and IGF-1. The data in people come from short studies in healthy adults.

before: General health check with a doctor
during: IGF-1 (one dose group in a study rose above the normal range)
Fasting glucose or HbA1c

items.name: Cabergoline
items.status_label: FDA-approved for high prolactin (hyperprolactinemia)
items.summary: A prescription pill that lowers high levels of the hormone prolactin by acting like dopamine on the pituitary gland. Approved for high prolactin, including from pituitary tumors that make it.

during: Echocardiogram every 6 to 12 months or as clinically indicated
Prolactin
Blood pressure

items.name: Cagrilintide
items.status_label: Investigational; CagriSema under FDA review
items.summary: An experimental, long-acting version of the hormone amylin. Tested for weight loss on its own and with semaglutide (as CagriSema). Not FDA-approved.

before: General health check: weight, blood pressure, HbA1c or fasting glucose, kidney function
during: Same general checks at regular visits
Resting heart rate

items.name: Canagliflozin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, heart and kidney risk
items.summary: A prescription pill, sold as Invokana, that lowers blood sugar and heart and kidney risks in type 2 diabetes. The anti-aging interest rests on a mouse study.

before: Potassium if kidney function is moderately reduced
during: Kidney function as needed (an early creatinine rise usually stabilizes)
Potassium if kidney function is moderately reduced
Digoxin levels if you take digoxin
Lithium levels if you take lithium
Ketones if ketoacidosis is suspected
Foot checks for sores, infection or new pain

items.name: Cerebrolysin
items.status_label: Not approved in the US; prescription drug abroad
items.summary: A mix of small peptides from pig brain. Prescribed abroad for stroke and dementia, and taken for focus and memory. Not approved in the US, and the evidence behind it is weak.

items.name: Clomiphene
items.status_label: FDA-approved for ovulation induction; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription fertility pill that triggers ovulation in women who don't ovulate regularly. Men also take it to raise their own testosterone, which it isn't approved for.

before: Men: morning total testosterone, LH, FSH and estradiol
Semen analysis if fertility is a goal
during: Men: testosterone, estradiol and hematocrit
Eye exam if vision changes occur
Men: IGF-1 (it can fall)

items.name: CoQ10
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A substance your body makes that helps cells produce energy. Taken for heart health, muscle aches from statins, migraine and energy.

items.name: Collagen peptides
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; not FDA-evaluated for these uses
items.summary: Collagen broken down into small pieces of protein. Taken by mouth, mainly for skin hydration, elasticity and wrinkles, and sometimes for joint symptoms.

items.name: Creatine monohydrate
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A compound your body makes and also gets from animal foods. Taken as a supplement to add strength and power for short, intense exercise.

before: Kidney function (creatinine with eGFR, or cystatin C) for older adults or people with medical conditions planning long-term use
during: Periodic kidney function checks in those higher-risk groups during long-term use; cystatin C or a measured GFR avoids the creatinine effect

items.name: Crystagen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A tiny peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted to support immunity in older people. The evidence is mainly small studies by its own developers.

before: Complete blood count with a white-cell breakdown

items.name: Curcumin
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; also a common spice
items.summary: The main yellow compound in turmeric, taken mostly for joint pain and inflammation. The evidence is still early, and turmeric supplements have been linked to rare liver injury.

items.name: DHEA
items.status_label: Supplement; prescription vaginal form approved
items.summary: A hormone your adrenal glands make, which the body turns into testosterone and estrogen. Sold as a supplement for libido, well-being and aging. The evidence is weak.

before: Breast and pelvic exams as recommended for age
Evaluation of any abnormal genital bleeding
during: Lipid panel

items.name: DSIP
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A small peptide, also called emideltide, first found in rabbit brain blood. People take it hoping to sleep better. The evidence that it works is weak.

before: General health check, including blood pressure

items.name: Dapagliflozin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for kidney disease, heart failure, diabetes
items.summary: A prescription pill, sold as Farxiga, that makes the kidneys pass extra sugar out in the urine. It treats type 2 diabetes and lowers kidney and heart failure risks.

before: Blood pressure and fluid status, especially in older adults, with kidney impairment or with diuretics
HbA1c or fasting glucose if you have diabetes
during: Kidney function as needed (a small dip in eGFR in the first two weeks is expected, then stabilizes)
Blood pressure, watching for low readings
Ketones if ketoacidosis is suspected, and considered in type 1 diabetes
Lithium levels if you take lithium

items.name: Dihexa
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding review pending
items.summary: A lab-made compound based on the peptide angiotensin IV, used to try to boost memory. It improved learning in rodents. FDA found no data on it in people.

items.name: Dulaglutide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes and heart-risk reduction
items.summary: A prescription GLP-1 injection, sold as Trulicity. It lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes and reduces the risk of heart attack and stroke.

before: Eye exam if you have diabetic retinopathy
during: HbA1c to track blood sugar
Blood glucose if also taking insulin or a sulfonylurea
Kidney function if you have kidney disease and severe vomiting or diarrhea
Eye checks if you have diabetic retinopathy
INR if taking warfarin

items.name: Dutasteride
items.status_label: FDA-approved for enlarged prostate; off-label for hair
items.summary: A prescription capsule that stops the body making the hormone DHT. Approved in the US for an enlarged prostate. Also used for male pattern hair loss, which it isn't approved for.

during: PSA: a new baseline after at least 3 months; any confirmed rise from the lowest value should be evaluated

items.name: Empagliflozin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease
items.summary: A prescription pill, sold as Jardiance, that makes the kidneys pass extra sugar out in the urine. It treats type 2 diabetes and lowers heart failure and kidney risks.

before: Blood pressure and fluid status, especially in older adults or with diuretics
HbA1c or fasting glucose if you have diabetes
during: Kidney function as needed (a small early dip in eGFR is expected and usually stabilizes)
Ketones if ketoacidosis is suspected, and considered in type 1 diabetes
Lithium levels if you take lithium
HbA1c to track blood sugar if you have diabetes

items.name: Enclomiphene
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: One of the two forms that make up the fertility drug clomiphene. Studied as a pill to raise men's own testosterone. Not approved in the US or Europe.

before: Morning total testosterone, LH and FSH
Semen analysis if fertility is a goal
during: Testosterone and estradiol
Hematocrit
PSA
IGF-1 (it fell in trials)

items.name: Epitalon
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding status under FDA review
items.summary: A tiny lab-made peptide from Russian aging research. People take it hoping to slow aging and restore their melatonin rhythms. The evidence in people is very thin.

before: General health check with a doctor, including up-to-date age-appropriate cancer screening
during: General health check

items.name: Estradiol
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription hormone
items.summary: The body's strongest estrogen. Prescribed mainly to ease hot flashes and vaginal symptoms of menopause, and to prevent bone loss after it.

before: Breast exam and mammogram as recommended for age
Triglycerides if they are known to be high
Evaluation of any unexplained vaginal bleeding
during: Breast exams and mammography as recommended
Blood pressure at regular intervals
Thyroid function in people on thyroid hormone
Endometrial sampling if unexplained bleeding occurs

items.name: Exemestane
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription pill that permanently blocks aromatase, the enzyme that makes estrogen. Approved for hormone-sensitive breast cancer after menopause. Studies in men are few and brief.

before: Pregnancy test if pregnancy is possible
during: Bone density at intervals
Men (off-label): testosterone and estradiol

items.name: Exenatide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes; brands discontinued
items.summary: A prescription GLP-1 medicine, first approved as Byetta in 2005, that lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes. The brand-name versions were discontinued in the US in 2024.

during: HbA1c to track blood sugar (worsening control can signal antibodies)
Blood glucose if also taking insulin or a sulfonylurea
Kidney function if vomiting or diarrhea is severe
INR more often if taking warfarin

items.name: FSH
items.status_label: FDA-approved biologics for female and male infertility
items.summary: A prescription fertility hormone, made in the lab and given by injection. Approved to trigger ovulation and for IVF in women and, with hCG, to start sperm production in men.

before: Men: testosterone, LH and FSH, to confirm low pituitary hormones rather than testicular failure
Thyroid, adrenal or pituitary tests if a disorder is suspected
during: Men: semen analysis and testosterone
Women: ovarian response monitoring by a fertility specialist

items.name: Finasteride
items.status_label: FDA-approved for hair loss and enlarged prostate
items.summary: A prescription pill that stops testosterone turning into the hormone DHT. Approved for male pattern hair loss and an enlarged prostate. Sexual and mood side effects are a known concern.

before: PSA, for men who have prostate cancer screening
during: PSA, read with the knowledge that finasteride lowers it by about half; a confirmed rise from the lowest value should be evaluated

items.name: Follistatin 344
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A natural protein that blocks myostatin, a brake on muscle growth. People take it to build muscle. In people, it has been tested as a gene therapy for muscle diseases.

before: General health check (complete blood count and metabolic panel) if a doctor is involved
Pituitary and sex hormone levels, which the gene-therapy trial monitored

items.name: GHK-Cu
items.status_label: Non-injectable compounding allowed; injectable under review
items.summary: A small peptide that binds copper, found naturally in human blood. Used in skin creams and injected for skin, hair and healing. That rests mostly on small cosmetic studies and animal studies.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: GHRP-2
items.status_label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
items.summary: A lab-made peptide that makes the body release growth hormone and raises appetite. Used in Japan as a diagnostic test, and sold elsewhere as a 'research chemical'.

before: General health check with a doctor
during: Fasting glucose or HbA1c
IGF-1

items.name: GHRP-6
items.status_label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
items.summary: An early lab-made peptide that makes the body release growth hormone by acting on the ghrelin receptor. Sold as a 'research chemical'. Studies in people are small and short.

before: General health check with a doctor
during: Fasting glucose or HbA1c
IGF-1

items.name: Glutathione
items.status_label: Compoundable while FDA evaluates; also a supplement
items.summary: An antioxidant your body makes. Taken by mouth or by IV for liver health, detox and skin lightening. Studies in people are small, and IV use has caused serious reactions.

before: Liver enzymes (ALT, AST) if used for liver disease
during: Liver enzymes (ALT, AST) if used for liver disease

items.name: Glycine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: An amino acid taken mainly to sleep better. The evidence is three small, very short trials in healthy adults.

items.name: Gonadorelin
items.status_label: No US product; compounding appears to be allowed
items.summary: A lab-made copy of GnRH, the brain hormone that tells the pituitary gland to release LH and FSH. Men take it to support the testicles. There is little evidence behind that.

before: Semen analysis if fertility is the goal
during: LH, FSH and testosterone or estradiol
Semen analysis when treating infertility

items.name: HGH Fragment 176-191
items.status_label: Not approved; sold as a research chemical
items.summary: A lab-made piece of the tail end of human growth hormone, sold as a 'research chemical' for fat loss. The evidence comes from animal studies of a related peptide.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: Hexarelin
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A lab-made relative of GHRP-6 that makes the body release growth hormone by acting on the ghrelin receptor. Sold as a 'research chemical'. The data in people come from a few small studies.

before: General health check with a doctor
during: Fasting glucose or HbA1c
IGF-1

items.name: Humanin
items.status_label: Not approved; not nominated for compounding
items.summary: A small peptide coded for in the DNA of mitochondria. It protects cells in lab and animal studies, and levels fall with age. It has not been tested as a treatment in people.

items.name: IGF-1 DES
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A shortened, stronger form of IGF-1, missing its first three amino acids. Sold as a 'research chemical' for muscle growth. The evidence is limited to lab studies.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: IGF-1 LR3
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A lab-made, stronger form of IGF-1 that escapes the proteins that normally hold IGF-1 in check. Sold as a 'research chemical' for muscle growth. The evidence is limited to lab studies.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: Ipamorelin
items.status_label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
items.summary: A small lab-made peptide taken to raise growth hormone, acting on the ghrelin receptor. Its only treatment trial, for bowel recovery after surgery, missed its main goal.

before: General health check with a doctor
during: IGF-1
Fasting glucose or HbA1c

items.name: Iron
items.status_label: Dietary supplement (child-poisoning warning)
items.summary: An essential mineral the body needs to make hemoglobin. Taken to prevent or treat iron deficiency and the anemia and tiredness it can cause.

before: Transferrin saturation or full iron studies if inflammation may make ferritin misleading
during: Complete blood count and ferritin to check the response

items.name: KPV
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA compounding decision pending
items.summary: A tiny piece of the hormone alpha-MSH, used for gut and skin inflammation. That rests on cell and animal studies. It has never been tested in people.

before: General health check (blood count and metabolic panel)

items.name: Kisspeptin-10
items.status_label: FDA Category 2: pharmacies may not compound it
items.summary: The smallest fully active piece of kisspeptin, a natural hormone that switches on the body's chain of reproductive hormones. Taken to raise testosterone and for sexual health.

during: LH and testosterone or estradiol, if a doctor is supervising use

items.name: L-theanine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; GRAS food ingredient
items.summary: An amino acid from tea leaves. Taken to feel calm without getting drowsy, to ease stress, and to improve sleep quality and focus.

items.name: LL-37
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding review pending
items.summary: A peptide your own immune and skin cells make to fight germs and steer inflammation. Taken for immune support and wound healing. The evidence in people is limited to leg-ulcer trials.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: Letrozole
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; other uses off-label
items.summary: A prescription pill that stops the body making estrogen. Approved for hormone-sensitive breast cancer after menopause. Also used to trigger ovulation and in men with low testosterone, both unapproved uses.

before: Pregnancy test if pregnancy is possible
Men (off-label): testosterone, estradiol, LH, FSH and semen analysis
during: Bone density at intervals
Cholesterol periodically
Men (off-label): testosterone, estradiol and semen analysis

items.name: Leuprolide
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription drug
items.summary: A prescription injection that switches off the body's sex hormones. Used for prostate cancer, endometriosis, fibroids and puberty that starts too early in children.

before: Blood glucose or HbA1c and a lipid panel
Bone density before any repeat course in women
ECG and electrolytes if heart risk factors are present
during: Testosterone and PSA periodically (prostate cancer)
Blood glucose or HbA1c and lipids
ECG and electrolytes periodically in people at risk
In children: LH or sex-hormone levels, height growth and bone age

items.name: Lion’s mane
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; also eaten as food
items.summary: An edible mushroom (Hericium erinaceus) taken for memory, focus and mood. Small trials in people show mixed results, and most of the evidence comes from lab and animal studies.

items.name: Liraglutide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for diabetes, heart risk and weight
items.summary: A prescription GLP-1 medicine that lowers blood sugar and appetite. Sold as Victoza for type 2 diabetes and as Saxenda for weight management.

during: Resting heart rate at regular visits
Blood glucose if also taking insulin or a sulfonylurea
Kidney function if vomiting or diarrhea is severe

items.name: Low-dose naltrexone (LDN)
items.status_label: Off-label; low-dose forms are compounded
items.summary: Naltrexone is an opioid-blocking drug for addiction. In much smaller amounts, people take it for chronic pain and inflammatory conditions, which it isn't approved for. Small trials have given mixed results.

before: Liver function tests (liver injury is a label warning for naltrexone)

items.name: MGF
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA Category 3, PEG-MGF under review
items.summary: A lab-made peptide based on a variant of the IGF-1 gene. Used for muscle growth, and banned in sport. Its role in the body is disputed.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: MK-677
items.status_label: FDA Category 2: pharmacies may not compound it
items.summary: An experimental drug taken by mouth that acts like the hormone ghrelin to raise growth hormone and IGF-1. Taken for muscle, sleep and recovery. FDA bars pharmacies from making it over a heart-failure risk.

before: General health check with a doctor, including fasting glucose

items.name: MOTS-c
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding status under FDA review
items.summary: A small peptide coded for in the DNA of mitochondria. People take it hoping to improve metabolism, exercise capacity and aging. Its effects have only been tested in rodents and cells.

before: General health check, including fasting glucose or HbA1c
during: General health check

items.name: Magnesium glycinate
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: The mineral magnesium bound to the amino acid glycine. Taken mainly for sleep and relaxation, and to top up magnesium intake.

before: Serum magnesium if you are starting long-term proton pump inhibitor treatment (FDA advises checking)
during: Periodic serum magnesium during long-term proton pump inhibitor use

items.name: Mazdutide
items.status_label: Not approved in the US; approved in China in 2025
items.summary: A drug that acts on two hormone receptors, GLP-1 and glucagon. Approved in China in 2025 for weight management and type 2 diabetes. Not approved in the US.

before: General health check: weight, blood pressure, HbA1c or fasting glucose, kidney and liver tests
during: Same general checks at regular visits
Resting heart rate

items.name: Melanotan I (afamelanotide)
items.status_label: FDA-approved implant for a rare light disorder (EPP)
items.summary: A lab-made version of alpha-MSH, the hormone that darkens skin. Approved as an implant for a rare disorder that makes people sensitive to light. Unlicensed Melanotan I products are used for tanning.

during: Full-body skin exam twice a year

items.name: Melanotan II
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding review pending
items.summary: An unapproved, lab-made version of a hormone, injected for tanning and sometimes for sexual arousal. Case reports link it to mole changes and serious side effects.

before: General health check including blood pressure
during: Regular skin checks for new or changing moles

items.name: Melatonin
items.status_label: Dietary supplement in the US; prescription elsewhere
items.summary: A hormone your brain makes in the dark to time sleep. Sold in the US as a supplement, mainly to fall asleep faster or ease jet lag.

items.name: Metformin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes; aging use off-label
items.summary: A prescription pill that lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes. Some people take it hoping to slow aging. It isn't approved for that, and it's unproven.

during: Kidney function (eGFR) at least once a year, more often in older adults
Complete blood count once a year
Vitamin B12 every 2 to 3 years
HbA1c to track blood sugar

items.name: Methylene blue
items.status_label: FDA-approved injection for methemoglobinemia only
items.summary: A blue dye that is also an approved hospital drug for a rare blood disorder. Now promoted for focus and energy. The evidence in people for those uses is thin.

before: G6PD test (G6PD deficiency rules it out)

items.name: Minoxidil
items.status_label: Topical OTC for hair loss; tablets Rx for blood pressure
items.summary: Sold over the counter as a scalp treatment for hereditary hair loss, and by prescription as a tablet for severe high blood pressure. Low-dose tablets are also used for hair, which they aren't approved for.

items.name: Modafinil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for sleep disorders; Schedule IV
items.summary: A prescription drug that keeps people awake, for narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift-work sleepiness. Also taken for focus, which it isn't approved for. In rested, healthy people its effects are small.

items.name: NAC (N-acetylcysteine)
items.status_label: Approved drug; supplement sales tolerated by FDA
items.summary: A modified form of the amino acid cysteine. Approved as an antidote for acetaminophen overdose and as a mucus thinner, and sold for decades as a dietary supplement.

items.name: NAD+
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; pharmacies may compound it
items.summary: A molecule your cells use to make energy. Given by IV drip or injection, or taken by mouth, by people hoping for more energy and slower aging. The evidence in people is minimal.

items.name: NMN
items.status_label: Dietary supplement since FDA's September 2025 reversal
items.summary: A building block your body uses to make NAD+ (full name: nicotinamide mononucleotide). Taken in hopes of slowing aging and boosting metabolism. Benefits in people are unproven.

items.name: NR (nicotinamide riboside)
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; GRAS notice for some foods
items.summary: A form of vitamin B3 that raises NAD+, a molecule cells use for energy. Taken in hopes of healthier aging. Trials show few clear health effects.

items.name: Omega-3 fish oil
items.status_label: Supplement; prescription forms FDA-approved
items.summary: Oils from fish, krill or algae that supply the omega-3 fats EPA and DHA. Taken mainly for heart health and to lower triglycerides.

during: INR at intervals for people taking warfarin

items.name: Orforglipron
items.status_label: FDA-approved for weight management (April 2026)
items.summary: A GLP-1 medicine you take as a pill, sold as Foundayo. Approved in April 2026 for weight management in adults with obesity, or with overweight and a related health problem.

before: Eye exam if you have diabetic retinopathy
during: Blood glucose if you have diabetes, especially with insulin or a sulfonylurea
Kidney function if vomiting or diarrhea is severe
Resting heart rate at regular visits
Eye checks if you have diabetic retinopathy

items.name: Ovagen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A short lab-made peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for the liver and digestive tract. Exactly what it is, and whether it helps people, are poorly documented.

before: General health check, including a liver panel (ALT, AST, bilirubin)

items.name: Oxytocin
items.status_label: FDA-approved injection for labor and delivery
items.summary: A hormone that makes the uterus contract. Approved as an injection to start or strengthen labor. Nasal sprays taken for mood or bonding have little evidence behind them.

during: Contractions and the baby's heart rate (in hospital)
Fluid balance and blood sodium during long infusions

items.name: PEG-MGF
items.status_label: Not approved; not eligible for pharmacy compounding
items.summary: A lab-made version of a short peptide from the IGF-1 gene, with a PEG chain attached. Promoted for muscle growth and repair. Never studied in people.

before: General health check (complete blood count and metabolic panel) if a doctor is involved

items.name: PT-141
items.status_label: Approved (Vyleesi) for low desire in premenopausal women
items.summary: A lab-made peptide, FDA-approved as Vyleesi for low sexual desire in women before menopause. Also used for libido and erections, which it isn't approved for.

before: Blood pressure check and a review of heart risk

items.name: Pancragen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A tiny peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for the pancreas and blood sugar. Tested in cells, monkeys and small studies in people.

during: Blood sugar checks if you take diabetes medicines

items.name: Pemvidutide
items.status_label: Investigational; phase 3 start not confirmed
items.summary: An experimental drug that acts on two hormone receptors, glucagon and GLP-1. Tested for weight loss, and now mainly for fatty-liver disease (MASH) and alcohol use disorder. Not FDA-approved.

before: General health check: weight, blood pressure, HbA1c or fasting glucose, kidney and liver tests
during: Same general checks at regular visits
Resting heart rate

items.name: Pentadeca Arginate
items.status_label: Not approved; not on any FDA compounding list
items.summary: A peptide described as a form of the experimental peptide BPC-157 (its arginine salt), used for injury healing. It has not been tested in published studies. Not FDA-approved.

items.name: Phentermine
items.status_label: FDA-approved for short-term weight loss; Schedule IV
items.summary: A prescription appetite suppressant related to amphetamine. Approved for short-term use alongside a weight-loss program. A Schedule IV controlled substance.

during: Blood glucose in people with diabetes, whose medicine needs may change

items.name: Pramlintide
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Symlin); reported discontinued in the US
items.summary: A lab-made form of the hormone amylin. Approved as Symlin for adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who use mealtime insulin. Reported discontinued in the US.

before: Recent home glucose readings and any history of low blood sugar
during: Blood glucose before and after meals and at bedtime, especially when starting or changing treatment
HbA1c

items.name: Pregnenolone
items.status_label: Supplement; FDA reviewing it for compounding
items.summary: A steroid the body turns into other hormones, including ones that act on the brain. Sold as a supplement, and studied in small trials for pain, schizophrenia and bipolar depression.

items.name: Probiotics
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: Live microorganisms, such as Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium and Saccharomyces boulardii. Taken mainly to prevent diarrhea from antibiotics and to ease gut symptoms.

items.name: Progesterone (micronized)
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription hormone (Prometrium)
items.summary: A prescription form of the natural hormone progesterone. Used mainly to protect the lining of the uterus in women taking estrogen after menopause, and to treat periods that have stopped.

before: Breast exam and mammogram as recommended for age
Evaluation of any unexplained vaginal bleeding
during: Yearly breast exam, pelvic exam and mammogram
Prompt evaluation of any unusual vaginal bleeding

items.name: Prostamax
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A short lab-made peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for prostate health. The published evidence is limited to lab studies on cells and DNA.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: Raloxifene
items.status_label: FDA-approved for women after menopause; not for men
items.summary: A prescription pill (a SERM) that lowers the risk of spine fractures and of breast cancer in women after menopause. Its label says it is not recommended for men.

before: Triglycerides, if they rose sharply on past estrogen therapy
Men (off-label): PSA, testosterone, LH and FSH
during: Bone density at intervals
Triglycerides in women whose triglycerides rose on estrogen
Men (off-label): PSA and testosterone

items.name: Rapamycin
items.status_label: FDA-approved transplant and LAM drug; not for aging
items.summary: A transplant drug (sirolimus) that holds back the immune system. It extends lifespan in mice, and is being studied in people as a possible way to slow aging.

during: Sirolimus blood (trough) levels
Lipid panel
Kidney function and urine protein
Blood glucose

items.name: Retatrutide
items.status_label: Investigational; not approved, not legal to compound
items.summary: An experimental Eli Lilly drug that acts on three hormone receptors (GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon). It is in late-stage obesity trials. Not FDA-approved.

before: General health check: weight, blood pressure, HbA1c or fasting glucose, kidney function
during: Same general checks at regular visits
Resting heart rate

items.name: Rhodiola rosea
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A cold-climate herb (golden root) taken to fight fatigue and stress and to lift mood. Trials are small and conflicting, and NIH says there isn't enough evidence.

items.name: SLU-PP-332
items.status_label: Not approved; experimental, animal studies only
items.summary: An experimental compound that copies some effects of exercise in mice by switching on estrogen-related receptors (ERRs). No studies in people have been published.

before: General health check (complete blood count and metabolic panel) if a doctor is involved

items.name: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3)
items.status_label: Cosmetic ingredient; not an approved drug
items.summary: A small lab-made peptide used in anti-wrinkle skin products. Marketed as a skin-applied alternative to Botox for expression lines.

items.name: SS-31
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Forzinity) for Barth syndrome only
items.summary: A lab-made peptide that targets mitochondria, where cells make energy. FDA-approved in 2025 as Forzinity, for Barth syndrome only. People also take it for aging and energy, based mostly on animal studies.

during: Complete blood count, since eosinophil counts often rose with longer use

items.name: Selank
items.status_label: Not approved; not eligible for compounding
items.summary: A small lab-made peptide based on tuftsin, a piece of an immune protein. Taken for anxiety and focus. The evidence in people is one small Russian study.

before: General health check with a doctor

items.name: Semaglutide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for diabetes, weight, heart, kidney, MASH
items.summary: The prescription GLP-1 medicine sold as Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy. Used to lower blood sugar in type 2 diabetes and to lose weight.

before: Eye exam if you have diabetic retinopathy
during: Blood glucose if also taking insulin or a sulfonylurea
Kidney function if vomiting or diarrhea is severe
Resting heart rate at regular visits
Eye checks if you have diabetic retinopathy

items.name: Semax
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; compounding decision pending
items.summary: A lab-made peptide based on a piece of the hormone ACTH. Registered in Russia as nasal drops, and taken for focus, memory and stroke recovery.

before: General health check with a doctor, including a review of bleeding risk

items.name: Sermorelin
items.status_label: Compounded by prescription; former approved drug
items.summary: A shortened copy of the brain hormone that tells the pituitary gland to release growth hormone. Once an approved drug. Now made by compounding pharmacies and used to raise growth hormone and IGF-1.

during: IGF-1
Fasting glucose or HbA1c

items.name: Sildenafil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for erectile dysfunction
items.summary: The prescription pill in Viagra (a PDE5 inhibitor), for erectile dysfunction. The same drug is also sold as Revatio for pulmonary arterial hypertension (high blood pressure in the lungs).

before: Morning total testosterone if low testosterone is suspected

items.name: Somatropin (HGH)
items.status_label: FDA-approved; illegal to distribute for anti-aging
items.summary: Lab-made human growth hormone. Prescribed for growth hormone deficiency and certain growth disorders. Distributing it for anti-aging or bodybuilding is a federal crime.

before: Cortisol if adrenal insufficiency is possible
during: IGF-1
Glucose periodically
Thyroid function periodically
Eye exams periodically

items.name: Spironolactone
items.status_label: FDA-approved for heart and fluid problems; acne off-label
items.summary: A prescription water pill for heart failure and high blood pressure. It also blocks male hormones, so it's used for acne and hair loss in women, which it isn't approved for.

during: Potassium within a week of starting or changing the dose, and regularly after
Kidney function, electrolytes, uric acid and blood glucose periodically

items.name: Survodutide
items.status_label: Investigational; not approved
items.summary: An experimental Boehringer Ingelheim drug that acts on two hormone receptors, glucagon and GLP-1. In phase 3 trials for obesity and fatty-liver disease. Not FDA-approved.

before: General health check: weight, blood pressure, HbA1c or fasting glucose, kidney and liver tests
during: Same general checks at regular visits
Resting heart rate

items.name: TB-500
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding not yet allowed
items.summary: A lab-made piece of the protein thymosin beta-4, promoted for injury and wound recovery. FDA found no studies of it in people.

before: General health check (complete blood count and metabolic panel) if a doctor is involved

items.name: Tadalafil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for ED and enlarged-prostate symptoms
items.summary: A prescription pill (a PDE5 inhibitor) for erectile dysfunction and for urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate. In trials, its effect on erections lasted up to 36 hours.

before: Morning total testosterone if low testosterone is suspected

items.name: Tamoxifen
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription SERM that treats hormone-sensitive breast cancer, including in men, and lowers the risk in high-risk women. Also used for male breast enlargement and infertility, which it isn't approved for.

before: Gynecological exam for women with a uterus
Cholesterol and triglycerides if already high
Men (off-label): testosterone, estradiol, LH and FSH
during: Complete blood count and liver tests periodically
Yearly gynecological exam
Eye exam if vision changes
Men (off-label): hormones, and semen analysis if fertility is the goal

items.name: Taurine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; common energy-drink ingredient
items.summary: An amino acid found in energy drinks and supplements, taken for energy and healthy aging. The lifespan gains seen in animals haven't been shown in people.

during: Blood pressure and blood sugar, if you take medicines for them

items.name: Telmisartan
items.status_label: FDA-approved for high blood pressure; aging off-label
items.summary: A prescription drug for blood pressure and heart protection. In lab studies it also partly turns on a metabolic switch (PPAR-gamma). Benefits for healthy aging are unproven.

during: Potassium and kidney function, especially with other drugs acting on the same hormone system
Lithium or digoxin levels if either is taken too

items.name: Tesamorelin
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Egrifta) for HIV-related belly fat
items.summary: A lab-made version of the brain hormone that triggers the release of growth hormone. FDA-approved to shrink excess deep belly fat in adults with HIV.

during: IGF-1 (the label suggests considering stopping for persistent large elevations)
Glucose or HbA1c periodically
Eye exams for retinopathy in people with diabetes

items.name: Testagen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A Russian supplement peptide from Khavinson's 'bioregulator' research, promoted for male reproductive health and testosterone. The evidence in people is one small study by its developers.

before: Morning total testosterone, with LH and FSH, if low testosterone is the concern
Semen analysis if fertility is the concern

items.name: Testosterone
items.status_label: FDA-approved for male hypogonadism; Schedule III
items.summary: A male sex hormone. Prescribed to men whose testosterone is low because of a problem with the testicles, the pituitary gland or the hypothalamus. A Schedule III controlled substance in the US.

before: Morning fasting total testosterone on two separate days
during: Testosterone and hematocrit at 3 to 6 months, at 12 months, then yearly
PSA and prostate exam 3 to 12 months after starting, then routine screening
Blood pressure and lipids periodically

items.name: Thymosin alpha-1
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A peptide that acts on the immune system. Sold abroad as Zadaxin, mainly for hepatitis B, and taken for immune support. FDA found there wasn't enough evidence for any use it reviewed.

before: Liver enzymes (ALT) and thyroid test (TSH), especially with viral hepatitis
during: Liver enzymes and TSH if used with viral hepatitis

items.name: Thymosin beta-4
items.status_label: Not approved; eye drops in phase 3 trials
items.summary: A natural protein promoted for injury recovery, based on animal studies. In people it has been tested as eye drops and a skin gel, with mixed results. Not approved, and not the same thing as TB-500.

before: General health check (complete blood count and metabolic panel) if a doctor is involved

items.name: Tirzepatide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, weight and sleep apnea
items.summary: The prescription injection sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound. It acts on two hormone receptors (GIP and GLP-1) to lower blood sugar and body weight.

before: Eye exam if you have diabetic retinopathy
during: Kidney function if vomiting or diarrhea is severe
Blood glucose if also taking insulin or a sulfonylurea
Eye checks if you have diabetic retinopathy
INR or drug levels if taking warfarin or another narrow-margin drug

items.name: Tongkat ali
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: Root extract of a Southeast Asian tree (Eurycoma longifolia), long used as an aphrodisiac and taken mainly to raise testosterone. The evidence comes from a few small trials.

before: Total testosterone, if you are taking it for suspected low testosterone

items.name: Tretinoin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for acne; one cream for fine wrinkles
items.summary: A prescription skin medicine for acne. One cream version is also approved to soften fine wrinkles, blotchy pigment and roughness on the face.

items.name: Triptorelin
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Trelstar, Triptodur)
items.summary: A prescription hormone drug that, with continued use, shuts down the body's testosterone and estrogen. Approved for advanced prostate cancer and for puberty that starts too early in children.

before: Testosterone (men) or LH and sex-hormone levels (children)
Blood glucose or HbA1c and a lipid panel
Blood pressure and a heart rhythm check if there are QT risk factors
during: Testosterone, to confirm it stays suppressed (men with prostate cancer)
Blood glucose or HbA1c, lipids and blood pressure, periodically
In children: LH and sex-hormone levels, height periodically, and bone age

items.name: Turkesterone
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A plant steroid from Ajuga turkestanica, promoted for building muscle. The few small studies in people found no effect, and products often contain less than the label says.

items.name: Vitamin B12
items.status_label: Supplement; injections and nasal gel by prescription
items.summary: An essential vitamin for nerves, red blood cells and DNA. Taken to prevent or treat deficiency, which is more likely with age, vegan diets and some medicines.

before: Methylmalonic acid, which NIH describes as among the most sensitive markers of B12 status
Homocysteine, which rises with low B12 but is less specific
during: Serum B12 to confirm that levels have normalized

items.name: Vitamin D3
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: The form of vitamin D your skin makes in sunlight. Taken to keep bones healthy and to correct or prevent low vitamin D levels.

items.name: Zinc
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: An essential mineral the body needs for immune function, wound healing and hundreds of enzymes. Taken mostly to shorten colds and support immunity.

items.name: hCG
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription biologic; not for weight loss
items.summary: A pregnancy hormone that acts like the hormone LH. Prescribed for men whose testicles are underactive because of a pituitary problem, for undescended testicles in boys, and to trigger ovulation.

before: Morning testosterone with LH and FSH, to confirm the cause of low testosterone
Semen analysis if fertility is the goal
during: Testosterone levels
Semen analysis if fertility is the goal

items.name: hMG
items.status_label: FDA-approved biologic for IVF; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription fertility injection with FSH and LH activity, purified from the urine of women past menopause. Approved for IVF. Also used in men to start sperm production, which it isn't approved for.

before: FSH (to rule out primary ovarian failure)
Evaluation of the male partner's fertility
Men (off-label): testosterone, LH, FSH and semen analysis
during: Ultrasound and estradiol levels to track ovarian response
Men (off-label): semen analysis and testosterone
